implementation_behavior_to_test: Generate declared category sets and ordered family telescopes. Accept exact sorts and arity. Reject unknown categories and mismatched argument vectors.
Generate ambient and introduced scopes independently. Require every introduced binder and forbid escaped arguments. Accept shared ancestors across distinct families.
Generate nested scopes with repeated spellings. Allocate distinct lexical identities and reject duplicate identities on one scope path.
Enter and leave nested binders. Resolve the nearest binder and restore the previous binding after exit.
Compare normalized rules with independently authored premise rules. Preserve each endpoint, ordinary child, constructor, and binder position.
Give ordinary bindings and distinct endpoint values to multiple premises. Preserve every binding outside generated targets.
Compare one explicit family with one ordinary transition premise. Reject a target that already has an input binding.
Generate signatures with differing category names and constructor arities. Preserve endpoint and parent types under zero, one, and multiple binders.
Apply injective renamings to lexical identities. Preserve admission and normalization structure. Compare capture behavior through the existing scope implementation.
Change one projection side, constructor position, ordinary variable, binder identity, or ordered argument. Reject each changed paired context.
Use repeated ordinary metavariables and distinct scoped values. Compare normalized matching and reconstruction with the original family context.
Generate declaration and occurrence rosters. Reject missing, repeated, unused, and undeclared families.
Normalize twice. Require exact equality after the first pass and require removal of every explicit family declaration and projection.
Generate collisions with ordinary variables, binder spellings, existing premise targets, and prior environment bindings. Keep all new sources and targets distinct.
Give each family a distinct child result. Preserve declaration order, execute every premise, and reconstruct one parent result in the original positions.
Compare generated requests with each declared family and its lexical occurrence. Preserve category, introduced scope, ambient scope, and declaration order.
Run existing rules without family declarations through normalization. Preserve exact identities, including rules whose ordinary sides differ.
Keep the authored context and premise sequence. Append typed source inputs and generated transition premises. Keep targets as derived variables.
Inject a late refusal into a rule and into a multi-rule batch. Preserve every original input. Publish only complete successful results.
Compare generated authored family rules with independent ordinary-premise rules across arbitrary signatures, declaration orders, nested scopes, and distinct endpoint values.
Use repeated constructor labels and equal sibling subtrees. Select each family by child path. Preserve the selected occurrence and reject overlapping or changed positions.

Generate authored spellings independently from lexical identities. Include unused binders, typed contexts, both patterns, and every structured nested premise read and declaration. Compare against an independent name visitor.

Compare names, sorts, roles, term edges, and premise edges with independent ordinary-premise rules. Preserve existing allocated prefixes. Check fresh allocation capacity and refusal, Input-to-Binder aliases, and conflicting sorts. Do not require unchanged inferred numeric IDs across whole-rule normalization.

Preserve unique binder spellings and their typed-context aliases and premise references. Encode repeated spellings only when all references occur in erased family arguments. Reject collisions in surviving ordinary variables, contexts, premise reads, transition targets, intrinsic outputs, and quantified parameters. Preserve direct bound-reference refusals and opaque guard payloads.

Compare checked monotone string allocation with a finite independent candidate oracle. Require exact reserved-name avoidance, advancing counters, binder/source/target separation, success when a representable free candidate exists, and atomic refusal at counter exhaustion.

Generate missing or mismatched child-sort evidence at different depths. Refuse descendant holes without re-enabling through inferred constructors. Preserve typed siblings, complete unknown-subtree census, and root projections. Compare eligible contexts with existing typed normalization.

Generate nested optional declarations with mixed parameter kinds. Compare every cached entry with the original iterator, including payload handles, optional flags, arity, and out-of-range access. Distinguish absent signatures from empty signatures.

Preserve existing success, refusal, and error locations after erasing diagnostic metadata. Generate repeated spellings at nonzero multiple-binder indices. Require the exact binder name, binder path, local index, and conflicting external location.

Generate complete ordinary type expressions and ordered family domains. Preserve ordinary payloads exactly. Admit Rewrite only at the terminal rewrite-context codomain. Reject families in domains, ordinary wrappers, equations, and intrinsic outputs. Compare canonical context transport with the original raw values. Preserve executable type refusals independently of syntax admission.

Preserve exact ordinary identifier and keyword spellings in context types. Apply the existing canonical identifier rules. Reject string literals, numeric literals, punctuation, and end-of-input. Keep bare constructor names as categories. Exercise every lexer keyword and generated identifiers through the actual source parser.

Compare actual generated DDL and structural lowering with independent complete type values. Preserve exact legacy outer encodings and canonical ordered children. Compare both output carriers, source parser agreement, admission, depth refusal, and cancellation cuts.

Check fresh custom kinds at priority zero against the actual lexer. Preserve old primaries, alternative order, and keyword reservation. Retain both bare and applied constructor readings through secondary capture. Preserve complete names and reject invalid lexical forms.

Generate distinct registered sort and constructor names. Exercise family domains, endpoints, and constructor contexts through the canonical adapter. Check exact registered identities and public rejection of duplicate signatures. Generate absent names in domains, endpoints, and constructors. Require public lowering refusal without a returned LanguageCore.

Generate heterogeneous constructor domains and codomains. Compare explicit families with independently authored transition-premise rules. Check wrong arity and wrong expected result refusal. Place one family at each ordered constructor argument. Compare compiled child sorts and runtime results against the independent ordinary rule. Reject out-of-range or extra arguments. Generate heterogeneous product factors and compare explicit-family compilation with ordinary rules. Check wrong arity refusal. Place families at each product factor and check exact ordered result reconstruction. Reject extra factors. Generate matching typed constructor, product, collection, and unary paths. Compare accepted explicit-family rules with independent ordinary-premise rules.

Generate registered unary functions with different domain and codomain names. Check nested binder arguments and body endpoint sorts against the ordinary-premise control. Require unchanged refusal for unary abstraction over a registered multiple function. Also retain existing executable multi context refusal.
Exercise List, Bag, Set, Map, and PathMap contexts. Compare child sorts with ordinary rules. Check non-PathMap mode refusal, wrong descriptor refusal, and missing PathMap Set key refusal.

Use unknown names where unary, collection, and product descriptors are required. Require refusal through the public compiler. Keep registered Syntax and Opaque endpoints eligible as complete family values. Refuse attempts to decompose them as functions, collections, or products. Place a family below a missing or incompatible edge and below a computational context. Require refusal even if a later descendant has a known constructor sort. Keep an independent typed sibling eligible.

Use different registered key and pair sorts. Compare Set-mode families with independent ordinary rules through the existing semantic transition matcher. Use heterogeneous registered key/value product factors. Compare Map-mode families with independent ordinary rules and exact result keys. Retain valid neutral-empty and remainder-only ordinary controls. Require refusal for neutral or absent-mode payloads through final LanguageCore validation.

Compare generated declaration rosters and substitution histories with an independent chronological map. Preserve latest root values, declaration order, unique IDs, all five roles, resolved variable chains, and absent or undeclared omissions.
Create actual fresh nested lexical scopes with reused numeric IDs. Verify nearest scope selection, parent scope selection, root fallback, local-only omission, and unchanged direct Ground root values.
Exercise first and later unresolved grounding, every paid work cut, and every cancellation cut. Require the exact error with no returned vector and unchanged input history.

Execute independent ordinary and explicit-family rules under nested binders through public canonical compilation and the transition matcher. Require exact reconstructed keys, binder values, ordered child receipts, and no-successor controls.
